Systemd is not Magic Security Dust

I always thought systemd was reaching out for simplified config. Nothing in their development cycle inherently produces less exploitable bugs, they are just looking at service management differently or at all in some of the cruft.

You can start a daemon as a non-root user, in a restricted filesystem namespace, with mandatory access control.

And systemd achieves this by having its own, root-level network stack, from which all other stacks are provisioned. The bootloader has a network stack. And a CLI. And a host of user-space daemons. It crosses every threshold of the OSI model that it can feasibly get its fingers into. So no, of course it doesn't, in any way, increase security.

Systemd is by far the greatest security risk the Linux world has ever unleashed upon itself. When the big one comes, and it will, it will make the Windows viruses of old look like childsplay.
